A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hadronic freeze-out curve is not an ad-hoc parameter but is a natural consequence of the chiral restoration and that the hadronic degrees of freedom are not a mere spectator of the chiral condensation but play an important role in the process.
the hadronic chemical freeze-out curve in the (T-μ)-plane can be explained within a consistent framework which is based on the chiral phase transition.
the hadronic freeze-out curve in the phase diagram is determined by the chiral transition and the chemical freeze-out mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chiral transition is a necessary, but not sufficient condition for the chemical freeze-out.
the chiral condensation plays a crucial role for the chemical freeze-out and that the pion and nucleon fluctuations are important for a quantitative understanding of this process.
